fields.value: The paper frames gaze as a nonverbal acknowledgment that projects the order of service provision and signals which requester will be served next.

quotes.text: In this situation, we found that the gaze of the nurses plays an important role to arrange the order of service provision.
In other words, the nurse successfully projects the order to the elderly visitors by only turning her gaze.
Based on these concerns, we proposed a new robot system that can display acknowledgements by turning its gaze toward each person who wants to initiate interaction.

fields.value: Gaze acknowledges a subsequent request, projects the service order, and communicates to the waiting person that they will be served next, allowing the robot to continue serving the first person while the second waits.

fields.value: Gaze acknowledgment improved perceived robot recognition and ease of calling; participants gave higher scores across all four questions, though satisfaction did not differ significantly. Without acknowledgment, participants repeated hand raises and some used emphatic waving or said “excuse me.” Impression ratings also suggested more positive evaluation with the nonverbal gesture.

quotes.text: Participants who experienced the robot gazing give higher scores for all questions. Particularly significant differences were found in questions 2 and 3 (p<0.05).

In the group of participants which experienced the robot without gazing, we observed some participants making emphatic gestures such as waving their hands widely and frequently, or issuing an utterance such as “excuse me.”
These results suggest that the CCR's nonverbal gesture may create a positive evaluative attitude.

This result therefore confirms that nonverbal communication by a service provider in a multi-party setting is crucial to create an atmosphere in which people can accept the situation and wait until they are served.

fields.value: CCR autonomously circulates while looking around, detects hand-raising requests using a body-mounted laser range finder and human-shape tracking, and, when a second request is detected en route to the first person, momentarily stops and turns its gaze toward the second person before continuing. The comparative experiment used WoZ to avoid request-recognition errors.

fields.value: CCR used a Segway RMP50 mobile platform, an upper body with eight arm-motion joints, and a pan-tilt mount in the neck for head movement.

quotes.text: We adapted a Segway mobile robot (RMP50 by Segway Japan) as the mobile platform so that the robot can move smoothly.
In the upper body 8 joints were installed to enable the robot to move its arms in a way similar to humans.
A pan-tilt mount (PTU-D46-17 by Directed Perception) was installed inside the neck for head motion.

fields.value: The authors developed a mobile care robot that acknowledges a second person’s request by turning its gaze toward them while it is serving someone else. In a two-person snack-delivery experiment, gaze acknowledgment improved perceived recognition and ease of calling, while satisfaction ratings did not differ significantly.

RQ1; RQ2; RQ3; RQ4; RQ5 — The paper describes gaze as a nonverbal signal that acknowledges requests and projects service order, tests its role and effects in a two-person interaction, details the sensing and gaze behavior, and specifies the robot platform and physical features.
